To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electron field emission (FE) from Si/SiO2/Si MLC is observed in a wide range of electric field (from 0.1 to 5 V/nm) and temperature (from 300 to 900K) at low voltages and currents.

the resonance-tunnel effect in field emission from silicon MLC is observed for the first time, the emission characteristics of MLC with quantum well (MQW) are different from those of the MLC with a single barrier (MSB), and the electron emission current from the MQW MLC is 1.5-2 times higher than that of MSB MLC.
(1) the field emission from MLCs with QW is a resonance-tunneling process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical and experimental investigations in electron field emission from Si-based resonance-tunnel structures.
the study of electron field emission (FE) properties of silicon-based resonance-tunneled MLC with QW.
the theoretical and experimental investigations on the resonance-tunnel field emission from silicon MLC with quantum wells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron transport in MLC with QW has been investigated and the electron emission from MLC with QWs have been observed.
the resonance-tunnel effect has been observed in the field emission from MLC with quantum well.
resonance tunneling in MLC with QW is a very promising way to enhance the electron field emission from cathodes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a new type of field electron emission from the MLC with quantum well has been found.
the field emission current from the silicon-based MLC is strongly dependent on the thickness of the silicon layer.
the MLC with QW have a higher current density than the MLC without QW, and the current density of the MLC with a single QW is higher than the one with multiple QWs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field emission current density from MLC with QW is much higher than that from MLC without QW.
the field emission from the QW is possible only at a certain voltage range, and the emission from the QWs can be suppressed at the voltages above the range.
the electron tunneling from QW in MLC is the key mechanism for the formation of the resonance peaks in the I–U characteristics.
